display.purpose: Hero headings only. Never used inside card components or body sections.

headline.purpose: Section headings, primary page titles. First-visible heading on any page section.

title.purpose: Sub-section headings, feature card titles at the top of the content hierarchy.

body.purpose: Primary prose. Cap line length at 65-75ch. Medium weight gives presence without heaviness.

label.purpose: Category tags, navigation labels, status chips. Always uppercase with 0.1em tracking.

shadows.name: nav-halo
shadows.purpose: Navigation bar scrolled state. Red-tinted ambient glow; marks the nav as the highest-elevation fixed surface.

shadows.name: mobile-nav-drop
shadows.purpose: Mobile navigation panel drop shadow. Directional; same hue as nav-halo.

shadows.name: portrait-lift
shadows.purpose: Portrait card resting state. The system's highest resting elevation; reserved for photographs of people.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Vertical and blog card hover state. Applied simultaneously with -4px Y translate.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Standard state transitions: button hover, nav scroll, color changes. Duration 200-300ms.

motion.name: ease-slide
motion.purpose: Button animate variant slide: arrow and text exchange. Duration 300ms.

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: Fastest state change: color, opacity, border micro-transitions.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Button hover, shadow appearance, scale transforms.

motion.name: duration-deliberate
motion.purpose: Card image reveals, divider expansion, grayscale-to-color transitions. The system's characteristic pace.

narrative.overview:
Studio 1947's design system is built around a single irreducible signal: the red thread that connects local knowledge to global consequence. This is not an accent color. It is the organizing logic of the system: structural, directional, sparing. The thread appears where something matters. A call to action, a hover state that transforms a card title, a 2px divider that scales from 48px to full width. Its restraint is the point.

The system operates on a near-white canvas tinted almost imperceptibly warm. Body backgrounds draw from #FFFAFA to #FFEAEA as a fixed gradient: not blank white, not gray. Everything is slightly alive, slightly warm. Primary text is not black but Ink (#383649): a dark slate with a faint purple-warm undertone. Surfaces feel printed, not rendered. Components are designed to feel like physical materials. Buttons are stamps. Cards are slabs. Hover states do not animate to be delightful; they move because something real is about to happen.

This system explicitly rejects: Webflow template friendliness; Linear/Stripe minimalism; generic agency portfolio patterns; consultant-corporate whitepaper aesthetics.
keyCharacteristics: One dominant signal: Signal Red (#D80000), used where it matters, never decoratively
Near-white warm canvas: body gradient from #FFFAFA to #FFEAEA, fixed in viewport
Ink not black: #383649 is the ground color for text and UI elements, warm-shifted
Flat by default: surfaces rest at the same elevation; interaction lifts
Variable type at scale: Bricolage Grotesque from 200 to 800 weight, with tight tracked headings and deliberate label uppercase
Motion as confirmation: 300-700ms ease-out transitions; GSAP power3.out for scroll reveals

rules.name: The One Thread Rule
rules.body: Signal Red (#D80000) occupies no more than 15% of any given screen by area. Its rarity is the mechanism. Used casually, it becomes decoration. Used deliberately, it becomes direction.

rules.name: The No Void Rule
rules.body: Pure black (#000000) and pure white (#FFFFFF) are not used on surfaces. Ink (#383649) is the darkest value; #FFFAFA is the lightest. Everything exists in warm light.

rules.name: The No Gradient Text Rule
rules.body: background-clip: text with a gradient value is prohibited. All text uses a single solid color. Hierarchy is communicated through scale, weight, and opacity. Gradient text exists in the codebase (the gradient prop on Typography); do not use it.

rules.name: The Three-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Headings always track at -0.02em. Labels always track at 0.1em in uppercase. Body and subtext have no explicit tracking. Three states, used consistently; no fourth tracking value is introduced.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as responses to state: hover, scroll position, or active interaction. A component that is always lifted has surrendered its ability to lift.

rules.name: The Red Halo Exception
rules.body: The only ambient shadow in the system is the navigation's red-tinted halo. It is the single instance of Signal Red used tonally on a structural element. This exception does not extend to cards, modals, dropdowns, or any other surface.

dos: Do use Signal Red (#D80000) as a state signal: hover transitions, expanding elements, active links, conversion actions. It is directional, not decorative.
Do use Ink (#383649) for all primary UI elements: button fills, nav text, body copy, borders.
Do maintain the warm canvas: place no component on pure white (#FFFFFF) or untinted gray. The minimum tint is #FFFAFA.
Do let images start in grayscale at reduced opacity and reveal color on hover. Depth is revealed through attention, not announced.
Do vary card sizes and internal structures. Three card formats coexist; they are not interchangeable.
Do animate with deliberate easing: power3.out and power2.out for scroll reveals; ease-out for state transitions. Duration range is 300-700ms.
Do cap body prose at 65-75ch line length.
Do apply product-register rules on /products/* routes: clearer hierarchy, reduced decorative intensity, task-first layout.
donts: Don't build Webflow-template patterns: rounded cards with icon + heading + body text repeated in a uniform grid, gradient CTA buttons, testimonial carousels with star ratings.
Don't apply Linear/Stripe minimalism: immaculate whitespace as primary aesthetic, single-accent at under 5%, system-font precision.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. All text uses a single solid color.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored stripe on cards, callouts, alerts, or list items.
Don't build identical card grids. Three cards of identical size with identical internal structure means the design problem has not been solved.
Don't use glassmorphism outside the Portrait Card frosted panel.
Don't use the hero-metric template: large number, small label, supporting stats row, gradient accent.
Don't use pure black (#000000) or pure white (#FFFFFF) on UI surfaces.
Don't rush motion: ease-in curves, elastic or bounce easings, and durations under 150ms feel cheap against this system.
Don't use modals for low-commitment or secondary content.
Don't use Teal (#00BCD4) on brand-register surfaces. Teal belongs to the product register.
